criteria.text: The response finds that the Bill of Sale defines 'Purchased Assets' as only assets located at the Seller Facility in Fort Collins, so the finished-kit inventory at the Reno, Nevada warehouse would not be conveyed to Soulor.
The response locates the Purchased Assets problem in Section 1 of the Bill of Sale.
The response explains why the narrower Bill of Sale definition of Purchased Assets matters to Soulor.
The response recommends a fix for the narrower Bill of Sale definition of Purchased Assets.

The response finds that the Bill of Sale's choice of Colorado law and exclusive Larimer County, Colorado forum conflicts with the APA's choice of Delaware law and the exclusive Delaware Court of Chancery forum.
hints: laws of the State of Colorado

criteria.text: The response locates the governing law and forum conflict in Section 7 of the Bill of Sale.
The response explains why the governing law and forum conflict matters to Soulor.
The response recommends a fix for the governing law and forum conflict.

The response finds that Pellwyn's consent to assignment of the Exclusive Reagent Supply Agreement is required but is omitted from the APA's Required Consents, so the APA does not make obtaining it a closing condition for Soulor.
The response locates the missing Pellwyn consent in the APA's Schedule 4.4 (Required Consents) or Section 7.2(c).
The response explains why the omission of Pellwyn's consent matters to Soulor.
The response recommends a fix for the omission of Pellwyn's consent.
The response states that under APA Section 10.4 the Bill of Sale controls the conveyance of title to the Purchased Assets.
The response is a memo that presents the issues individually, giving for each its location (document and section), why it matters to Soulor, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that the APA's 'wherever located' definition of Purchased Assets governs the conveyance, so the Reno warehouse inventory is transferred to Soulor under the current documents.
